title: Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Chemical Reactions Worksheets (Word Equations, Conservation of Mass)
standard_text: Chemical reactions as the rearrangement of atoms; representing chemical reactions using formulae and using equations; combustion, thermal decomposition, oxidation and displacement reactions; defining acids and alkalis in terms of neutralisation reactions; what catalysts do; energy changes on changes of state (qualitative); exothermic and endothermic chemical reactions (qualitative); the conservation of mass in changes of state and chemical reactions.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on chemical reactions: signs of a reaction, word and symbol equations, conservation of mass, combustion, thermal decomposition, oxidation, exothermic and endothermic. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Mass is conserved; reactions can warm or cool the surroundings.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged to make new substances.

  • Signs: gas, colour change, temperature change, precipitate, light.
  • Mass is conserved. If a gas escapes from an open container, the mass seems to fall.
  • Types: combustion, thermal decomposition, oxidation, neutralisation, displacement. Exothermic reactions warm the surroundings; endothermic ones cool them.
Example

12 g magnesium + 8 g oxygen → ?

12 + 8

Answer: 20 g magnesium oxide

Example

Copper carbonate heated → copper oxide + carbon dioxide. Type?

Heat breaks one compound

Answer: thermal decomposition

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mass is lost when something burns.
  • Thinking melting is a chemical change.
  • Thinking endothermic reactions get hotter.

faq.q: How do you know a chemical reaction has happened?
faq.a: A new substance forms. Signs include fizzing, a colour change, a temperature change, a precipitate or light.

faq.q: Why does a burning candle seem to lose mass?
faq.a: The carbon dioxide and water vapour it makes escape into the air. If they were collected, the total mass would be the same.
A reaction where heat breaks one compound into simpler substances, for example calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide.
